**Designing 4-bit carry-select block RTL**

**Analyzing carry-lookahead adder logic**

{
  "candidate_rtl": "module alu_64bit(
    input [63:0] a, b,
    input [2:0] Oper,
    output reg [63:0] sum
);
    wire is_arith = ~Oper[2] & ~(Oper[1] & Oper[0]);
    wire is_sub   = Oper[1] ^ Oper[0];
    wire swap_ab  = ~Oper[2] & Oper[1] & ~Oper[0];

    wire [63:0] arith_x = swap_ab ? b : a;
    wire [63:0] arith_base_y = swap_ab ? a : b;
    wire [63:0] arith_y = is_sub ? ~arith_base_y : arith_base_y;
    wire arith_cin = is_sub;

    wire [63:0] p = arith_x ^ arith_y;
    wire [63:0] g = arith_x & arith_y;
    wire [64:0] c;

    assign c[0] = arith_cin;

    genvar blk;
    generate
        for (blk = 0; blk < 16; blk = blk + 1) begin : CLA_BLOCK
            localparam integer B = 4 * blk;
            assign c[B+1] = g[B] |
                            (p[B] & c[B]);
            assign c[B+2] = g[B+1] |
                            (p[B+1] & g[B]) |
                            (p[B+1] & p[B] & c[B]);
            assign c[B+3] = g[B+2] |
                            (p[B+2] & g[B+1]) |
                            (p[B+2] & p[B+1] & g[B]) |
                            (p[B+2] & p[B+1] & p[B] & c[B]);
            assign c[B+4] = g[B+3] |
                            (p[B+3] & g[B+2]) |
                            (p[B+3] & p[B+2] & g[B+1]) |
                            (p[B+3] & p[B+2] & p[B+1] & g[B]) |
                            (p[B+3] & p[B+2] & p[B+1] & p[B] & c[B]);
        end
    endgenerate

    wire [63:0] arith_sum = p ^ c[63:0];
    wire [63:0] logic_sum =
        (Oper == 3'b011) ? (a | b) :
        (Oper == 3'b100) ? (a & b) :
        (Oper == 3'b101) ? (a ^ b) :
        (Oper == 3'b110) ? ~(a ^ b) :
                           64'b0;

    always @(*) begin
        if (is_arith)
            sum = arith_sum;
        else
            sum = logic_sum;
    end
endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The suspected critical path is the 64-bit arithmetic carry propagation. The original RTL contains three arithmetic modes, including both subtraction directions, and exposes a 65-bit arithmetic assignment internally; although source-level expressions do not prove the final mapped structure, this is evidence that arithmetic carry logic is a plausible bottleneck. The fixed Yosys/ABC flow must confirm whether the mapped netlist is actually carry-chain dominated.",
  "rewrite": "Use one shared add/sub datapath with operand swapping and conditional inversion, then replace a purely serial 64-bit carry recurrence with sixteen explicit four-bit carry-lookahead blocks. The logic operations remain separate and are selected only at the output. This preserves modulo-2^64 arithmetic while reducing the longest arithmetic carry dependency from bit-by-bit propagation to block-to-block propagation with four-bit local lookahead.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Hypothesis: shorter maximum data arrival on arithmetic cases if the baseline maps to a substantially serial carry path. The gain is expected to be moderate rather than guaranteed because ABC may already recognize and optimize the original arithmetic, and the added operand/output selection logic may become limiting. Timing, area, slew, capacitance, and equivalence must be measured under the specified flow.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "The explicit lookahead equations add propagate/generate and wide-AND/OR logic, so mapped area and fanout may increase. Sharing the add/sub datapath avoids separate arithmetic implementations and may offset part of that cost. The candidate is acceptable only if mapped area remains at or below 13098.437440 um^2 and all required max-slew and max-capacitance checks have zero violations.",
  "functional_boundaries": "For Oper=000 the result is a+b; 001 is a-b; 010 is b-a; 011, 100, 101, and 110 are OR, AND, XOR, and XNOR respectively; all other Oper values produce zero. Arithmetic carries beyond bit 63 are discarded exactly as in the original output behavior. No clock, state, input restriction, don't-care, or timing assumption is introduced. The internal carry is not an output and does not alter the externally observable 64-bit result."
}
